title: Top Local Payment Methods in Vietnam: How Vietnamese Pay
summary: From bank transfers and VietQR to MoMo, ZaloPay and cards, see how Vietnamese consumers pay online and in store, and how to accept them.
body_markdown:
Vietnam is moving from cash to digital faster than almost any market in the region. Non-cash payments grew 42.21% in transaction count and 22.65% in value in 2025, and QR code payments jumped 50.94% in volume and 124.06% in value, according to the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) (


[VnEconomy](https://en.vneconomy.vn/non-cash-payments-reach-28-times-gdp-in-2025.htm) ). ATM transactions fell 17.30% over the same period, a clear sign that people are withdrawing less cash.


Online, the shift is already well advanced. By the end of 2024, 66.8% of e-commerce orders in Vietnam were paid without cash, almost 27% more than two years earlier, according to the State Bank of Vietnam citing a[Ministry of Industry and Trade survey](https://vneconomy.vn/gia-tri-thanh-toan-khong-dung-tien-mat-nam-2025-gap-khoang-28-lan-gdp.htm)


. The government is targeting 80% by[2030.](https://haiquanonline.com.vn/den-nam-2030-thanh-toan-khong-tien-mat-chiem-80-tong-so-don-hang-thuong-mai-dien-tu-198391.html&link=autochanger)


Cash is still part of the picture. It accounted for about one-third of in-store spending in 2025, and cash on delivery made up[16% of e-commerce value](https://fintechnews.sg/128337/e-commerce/southeast-asia-payment-methods-2026-global-payments-report/)


. A good Vietnamese checkout makes it easy for these shoppers to pay upfront instead.


This guide walks through the four payment method categories that matter most, who uses each one, and when to offer it. Each section links to our in-depth guide for that category.

**Payment method** **Popular options** **Best for** **How the customer pays**

##


## **1. Bank transfer and VietQR: paying straight from the bank app**


Bank transfers are the largest online payment method in Vietnam, at 28% of e-commerce value in 2025 (


[Xendit](https://www.xendit.co/en-vn/blog/e-wallets-in-vietnam-a-complete-guide-to-accepting-digital-wallet-payments-for-businesses/) ). They run on NAPAS, the National Payment Corporation of Vietnam, whose 24/7 instant transfer service lets money move between banks in seconds.


VietQR has made these transfers much easier. It is the national QR standard for bank transfers and payments, so instead of typing account numbers, a customer simply scans a code in their banking app. That convenience is behind the QR boom in the SBV’s 2025 figures. NAPAS is now extending QR to merchant payments and linking it with Thailand, Cambodia and Laos for cross-border payments (


[Vietnam Economic Times](https://en.vneconomy.vn/opportunities-for-qr-payment-growth.htm) ).


For online checkout, the key is making sure each transfer is matched to the right order. A virtual account does this by giving each customer or order its own account number, so payments are identified and confirmed automatically, with no screenshots of transfer slips to check.


How it works: the customer receives a unique account number at checkout and pays it from their banking app. The payment is identified and confirmed as soon as it arrives.


When to offer it: for higher-value purchases, B2B invoices, education, insurance, and any checkout where customers prefer to pay from their bank. With Xendit, you can accept bank transfers into virtual accounts at six Vietnamese banks, including BIDV and VPBank, from VND 10,000 to just under VND 500 million per transaction.


## **2. E-wallets: the fastest-growing way to pay**


E-wallets are central to everyday spending in Vietnam, from food delivery and ride-hailing to bills and online shopping. They are also heavily promotion-driven: 65% of Vietnamese consumers cite promotions as a key reason to use a wallet (


[Decision Lab](https://www.decisionlab.co/blog/demystifying-the-rise-of-e-wallets-in-vietnam) , via


[Xendit’s e-wallet guide](https://www.xendit.co/en-vn/blog/e-wallets-in-vietnam-a-complete-guide-to-accepting-digital-wallet-payments-for-businesses/) ). Vietnam has a broad, competitive wallet market, with 49 licensed operators as of 2025 (


[Fintech News Singapore](https://fintechnews.sg/128337/e-commerce/southeast-asia-payment-methods-2026-global-payments-report/) ).


The wallets that matter most:


- MoMo: the largest wallet by usage, with broad reach across online and offline spending.


- ZaloPay: built into Zalo, one of Vietnam’s most used messaging apps, and strong for everyday payments and transfers.


- ShopeePay: the go-to wallet for Shopee shoppers and promo-driven e-commerce purchases.


- VNPT Money and Viettel Money: telco-backed wallets linked to two of Vietnam’s major mobile networks.


- Appota: a wallet with roots in gaming payments, now used for bills, transfers and online shopping.


How it works: the customer picks a wallet at checkout, is redirected to the app, and confirms the payment. Confirmation is instant.


When to offer it: for consumer-facing businesses, especially gaming and digital goods, F&B, fashion and anything bought on mobile. With Xendit, you can accept ZaloPay, ShopeePay, VNPT Wallet and Appota, from VND 1,000 to VND 500 million per transaction, with refunds supported.


***Also read:***[E-Wallets in Vietnam: A Complete Guide to Accepting Digital Wallet Payments for Businesses](https://www.xendit.co/en-vn/blog/e-wallets-in-vietnam-a-complete-guide-to-accepting-digital-wallet-payments-for-businesses/)


## **3. Credit and debit cards: domestic, international and contactless**


Vietnam has its own domestic card network run by NAPAS, while international Visa, Mastercard and JCB cards are used for online shopping, travel, subscriptions and cross-border purchases. Contactless is spreading fast too: in April 2025, NAPAS brought Apple Pay’s Tap to Pay to more than 80 million contactless cardholders (


How it works: online, the customer enters card details and usually completes a 3D Secure check with their bank. Cards can also be saved for one-click and recurring billing.


When to offer it: for SaaS and subscriptions, travel and hospitality, international customers, and higher-value retail. With Xendit, you can accept Visa, Mastercard, and JCB, charge saved cards for recurring payments, and take Apple Pay on payment links.


***Read also:***[Credit Cards in Vietnam: A Complete Guide for Businesses Accepting Card Payments](https://www.xendit.co/en-vn/blog/credit-cards-in-vietnam-a-complete-guide-for-businesses-accepting-card-payments/)


## **4. Cash on delivery: still common, and worth shrinking**


Cash on delivery still made up 16% of e-commerce value in 2025 (


[Fintech News Singapore, citing GPR 2026](https://fintechnews.sg/128337/e-commerce/southeast-asia-payment-methods-2026-global-payments-report/) ), especially among rural customers and first-time online shoppers who want to see the goods before paying. For merchants, COD brings failed deliveries, returns and cash-handling costs.


When to offer it: only where your customers still expect it. The better long-term move is to make prepayment easy with bank transfers and e-wallets, and to reward it with small discounts or faster shipping, so fewer customers need COD at all.


## **How to choose the right payment mix**


There is no single best method; the right mix depends on what you sell, your average order value, and whether customers pay once or repeatedly. As a baseline, bank transfers plus the major e-wallets reach most Vietnamese online shoppers, and cards add the higher-value and international customers.


**Business type** **Start with** **Add next**

A few practical rules help whichever mix you choose. Put bank transfer and the most popular wallets first on mobile. Nudge COD customers toward prepayment with small incentives. Track success and drop-off rates per method, then add or reorder options based on what your own customers use.

## **Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)**


**What is the most popular online payment method in Vietnam?**


Bank transfers led e-commerce in 2025 at 28% of transaction value, helped by VietQR and NAPAS instant transfers. E-wallets are growing fastest and are forecast to reach 38% of e-commerce value by 2030.


**What is VietQR?**


VietQR is Vietnam’s national QR standard for bank transfers and payments, run through NAPAS. Customers scan a VietQR code in their banking app instead of typing account details, and the transfer arrives instantly.


**Which e-wallets should I accept in Vietnam?**


MoMo has the broadest reach, ZaloPay is strong for everyday payments, and ShopeePay suits promo-driven e-commerce. Through Xendit, you can accept ZaloPay, ShopeePay, VNPT Wallet and Appota through one integration.


**Is cash on delivery still necessary in Vietnam?**


COD was still 16% of e-commerce value in 2025. Offering bank transfer and e-wallets, and rewarding customers who prepay, helps reduce your reliance on it.


**Which methods support recurring payments?**


Saved cards are the main option for recurring billing through Xendit in Vietnam. Xendit’s Vietnamese e-wallets and bank transfers are set up for one-time, customer-initiated payments.


**Can a business outside Vietnam accept these payment methods through Xendit?**


Vietnam has strict foreign exchange and capital rules, so card acceptance and local payment methods through Xendit Vietnam are generally for businesses with an entity in Vietnam. If you are based elsewhere,


[contact our team](https://www.xendit.co/en/contact/contact-sales/) to discuss your options.
